items.label: f01-best-score-disagree
items.front: Why can the recipe page's 'best cook' and the dish page's best_score disagree?
items.back: Best cook picks the single log with the highest cookScore (mean of taste and texture, effort excluded; ties go to the most recent via strict >). The dish best_score averages taste over all logs and texture over all logs, then means those two averages - a different aggregate.

items.label: f03-ref-not-state-guard
items.front: Cmd+Enter in the cook-log editor bypasses the disabled Save button, and save() (CookLogEditor.tsx:56) has no guard. Why would adding if (saving) return; still not fully stop a double submit?
items.back: Two keydown events in the same tick both read the old state value before React re-renders. Use a ref (inFlight = useRef(false)) that is checked and set synchronously.

items.label: f02-javascript-href
items.front: source_url is stored unchecked and rendered as <a href> (RecipePage.tsx:120-121). What is the risk and fix?
items.back: A javascript: URL is clickable - React 18 only logs a warning. Validate the scheme (http/https only) at the request boundary, and render untrusted URLs defensively; high severity once the app is multi-user.

items.prompt: Dish and recipe deletes collect photo filenames inside the transaction and remove files after commit. What goes wrong with the cook-log delete, which removes files inside the transaction?

choices.text: SQLite locks the photo files, so fs.rm fails every time inside it
The files are never deleted, because fs.rm is skipped on rollback
Nothing: fs.rm is asynchronous, so it always runs after the commit
A rollback leaves rows pointing at photo files that no longer exist

choices: SQLite locks the photo files, so fs.rm fails every time inside it
The files are never deleted, because fs.rm is skipped on rollback
Nothing: fs.rm is asynchronous, so it always runs after the commit
A rollback leaves rows pointing at photo files that no longer exist

items.explanation: A transaction cannot cover files on disk. Deleting after commit means a failure leaves an orphan FILE rather than a dangling ROW - the safer direction (review finding 1).

items.prompt: Why is the simple BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK tx(fn) helper safe in THIS app but not something to copy to an async PostgreSQL driver unchanged?

choices.text: SQLite serializes every write anyway; the transaction is not really needed here
PostgreSQL drivers do not support issuing ROLLBACK from inside a try/catch block
It relies on a synchronous single connection; async drivers need a client per transaction
The helper is re-entrant on SQLite but not on PostgreSQL, so nesting would break

choices: SQLite serializes every write anyway; the transaction is not really needed here
PostgreSQL drivers do not support issuing ROLLBACK from inside a try/catch block
It relies on a synchronous single connection; async drivers need a client per transaction
The helper is re-entrant on SQLite but not on PostgreSQL, so nesting would break

items.explanation: fn cannot await, so no other request runs mid-transaction. The helper is also NOT re-entrant: a nested tx would issue a second BEGIN and SQLite would throw.

items.prompt: A user searches for: half-and-half cre. How does toFtsQuery shape that input for FTS5?

choices.text: One quoted phrase covering the whole input
Split on hyphens too, with a prefix * on every term
Each term quoted, with a prefix * on the last term only
The raw text, passed through to MATCH unchanged

choices: One quoted phrase covering the whole input
Split on hyphens too, with a prefix * on every term
Each term quoted, with a prefix * on the last term only
The raw text, passed through to MATCH unchanged

items.explanation: It builds "half-and-half" "cre"*: double quotes are stripped, each whitespace-separated term is wrapped in quotes (so don't or half-and-half is not parsed as FTS syntax), and * is added to the last term for prefix matching. A query that still fails to parse returns [] rather than a 500.
